netdbg - debug engine API

The extension talks to its debug engine, netdbg, with the Debug Adapter Protocol (DAP) over the engine's stdin and stdout. Between VS Code and the engine sits the extension's DAP relay (DapProxy), which adds logpoints, hit counts, Step Into Specific, the exception log, the SQL log and more on top of what the engine offers.

VS Code  <-- DAP -->  DapProxy (extension)  <-- DAP over stdin/stdout -->  netdbg.exe (x86 or x64)

engine marks messages that cross the engine boundary; extension relay marks messages the relay handles or sends itself (they never reach the engine). The engine of the program's bitness is started: ICorDebug needs a debugger of the same bitness as the program.

Generated from src/engineProtocol.ts by npm run docs:api; the same data as JSON Schema is in engine-api.json.

Starting the engine

Argument / variableMeaning
--interpreter=vscodeDAP over stdin / stdout (the default).
--log=<file>Writes the DAP traffic and the engine's own log, flushed per line (setting netdbg.trace).
--mcp-listenAlso accepts MCP on 127.0.0.1 with a token, and sends netdbg.mcpEndpoint (setting netdbg.mcp.enabled). The tools drive this session; VS Code follows through the usual DAP events.
--mcp-connect[=<enginePid>]Not used by the extension: run by AI clients outside VS Code, a stdio MCP server that relays to the latest engine started with --mcp-listen (or the given one).
NETDBG_SYMBOL_DIRSEnvironment variable: folders (separated by ;) searched first for PDBs, by module MVID (downloaded symbols).

launch arguments

Arguments of launch as the engine receives them. The extension resolves launch.json first: a .dll program becomes program: <dotnet.exe of the chosen bitness>, args: [<dll>, ...], and a .NET Framework exe gets __dotnetFramework. launch.json properties that only the extension reads (architecture, sourceFileMap, sourceSearchPaths, processName, waitTimeout) are not listed here.

FieldTypeDescription
programstringFull path of the exe to start (a .NET apphost, a .NET Framework exe, or dotnet.exe). Not needed with dumpPath.
dumpPathoptionalstringOpen this crash dump (.dmp with full memory) instead of starting a program (read only; capability netdbgSupportsDumps). The engine must have the bitness of the dumped process (the extension chooses it; a 32-bit process written as a 64-bit dump counts as x86). After configurationDone the engine sends process (without systemProcessId; dumpProcessId is the number in the dump) and stopped (exception on the thread that was throwing, else pause, with the description Crash dump). continue, the steps, pause, goto, setVariable, setExpression, netdbg.applyChanges, netdbg.freezeThread, netdbg.makeObjectId, netdbg.processUsage and expressions that run code are refused with the reason.
argsoptionalstring[]Command-line arguments.
cwdoptionalstringWorking directory of the program.
envoptional{ [name]: string | null }Environment variables added for the program. null removes a variable.
stopAtEntryoptionalbooleanStop at the first line of the user's Main (also for async Main).
justMyCodeoptionalbooleanOnly modules with symbols, without DebuggerNonUserCode / DebuggerHidden / DebuggerStepThrough, are user code (default true).
enableStepFilteringoptionalbooleanStep over property accessors and operators when stepping in (default true).
expressionEvaluationOptionsoptionalExpressionEvaluationOptionsOptions for evaluating expressions.
editAndContinueoptionalbooleanEdit and Continue (default true): modules of a Debug build with symbols are loaded so that netdbg.applyChanges can update them. The extension sets it from netdbg.editAndContinue.enabled unless launch.json does.
decompileoptional"app" | "off"Assemblies of the application without symbols are decompiled to C# by the engine (app, the default), or not (off). See netdbg.decompile.
sqlLogoptionalboolean | objectSQL log: read the commands the program runs through ADO.NET at the provider, without stopping (netdbg.sqlExecuted). methods replaces the provider methods (Namespace.Type.Method). The extension sets it from netdbg.sqlLog.* unless launch.json does.
exceptionLogoptionalboolean | objectException log: record every thrown exception, also those that do not stop the program (netdbg.exceptionThrown); snapshot takes the stack and locals at the throw (default true). The extension sets it from netdbg.exceptionLog.*.
uiFreezeoptionalboolean | objectUI freeze watch (default on, 2000 ms): a UI thread that does not answer window messages for thresholdMs while the program runs pauses it there (netdbg.uiFrozen, then stopped with reason pause). The extension sets it from netdbg.uiFreeze.*.
coverageoptionalboolean | objectCode coverage: count the lines and branches the program runs (netdbg.coverageChanged, netdbg.coverage); the Cobertura XML and an HTML report of the sources (<name>.coverage.html beside it) are written when the session ends, into folder (absolute) or %LOCALAPPDATA%\netdbg\coverage. The extension sets it from netdbg.coverage.* unless launch.json does.
childProcessesoptional"record" | "follow" | "off"Processes the program starts with Process.Start: record (default) logs them (netdbg.childProcess), follow also suspends a .NET child and sends the reverse request startDebugging (attach with processId and __resumeChild) so that the client debugs it in its own session, off ignores them.
__dotnetFrameworkoptionalbooleanSet by the extension when program is a .NET Framework exe: the engine starts it with the .NET Framework CLR (no .NET runtime needed).
Example
{
  "type": "request",
  "seq": 2,
  "command": "launch",
  "arguments": {
    "program": "",
    "dumpPath": "",
    "args": [
      ""
    ],
    "cwd": "",
    "env": {},
    "stopAtEntry": false,
    "justMyCode": false,
    "enableStepFiltering": false,
    "expressionEvaluationOptions": {
      "allowImplicitFuncEval": false
    },
    "editAndContinue": false,
    "decompile": "app",
    "sqlLog": false,
    "exceptionLog": false,
    "uiFreeze": false,
    "coverage": false,
    "childProcesses": "record",
    "__dotnetFramework": false
  }
}

attach arguments

Arguments of attach. The process must have its runtime (coreclr.dll or clr.dll) loaded and be of the engine's bitness.

FieldTypeDescription
processIdnumber | stringProcess id. A string is accepted too (${command:pickProcess} returns one).
justMyCodeoptionalbooleanAs in launch.
enableStepFilteringoptionalbooleanAs in launch.
expressionEvaluationOptionsoptionalExpressionEvaluationOptionsAs in launch.
decompileoptional"app" | "off"As in launch (the application's folder is the folder of the process's exe).
sqlLogoptionalboolean | objectAs in launch.
exceptionLogoptionalboolean | objectAs in launch.
uiFreezeoptionalboolean | objectAs in launch.
coverageoptionalboolean | objectAs in launch.
childProcessesoptional"record" | "follow" | "off"As in launch.
__resumeChildoptionalbooleanSet by the parent's engine in its startDebugging request: the process is a child it suspended before its runtime started. The engine registers for the runtime's start and then resumes it (a .NET Framework child is resumed and attached once its runtime has loaded).

Standard DAP requests

The requests VS Code and the relay use, with what the extension relies on beyond the DAP specification.

CommandHandled byNotes
initializeengineAnswers with the capabilities below, then sends initialized. Reads supportsInvalidatedEvent.
launchengineChecks the program (exists, bitness of the engine, .NET Framework 4.x) and remembers it; starts it at configurationDone.
attachengineChecks the process (runtime loaded, bitness of the engine); attaches at configurationDone.
configurationDoneengineStarts or attaches, then sends process.
setBreakpointsengine extension relaycondition is a C# expression evaluated in the stopped program, or a marker (#once, #after File.cs:12, #changed expr, #caller A, B). The engine also judges hitCondition (N, ==N, >=N, >N, %N) and logMessage ({expr}, $FUNCTION, $TID, #track:, #timer-start: / #timer-end:). column (1-based) binds that statement when the line has several; omitted or 0 binds the first, and the answer then has column and endColumn. The relay maps paths.
setFunctionBreakpointsengineType.Method, Method, Namespace.Type.Method (all overloads). anyCode: true binds outside user code too.
setExceptionBreakpointsengine extension relayFilters all and user-unhandled; filterOptions[].condition is A, B or !A, B (type names).
exceptionInfoengineexceptionId is CLR/<type>, breakMode always / unhandled / userUnhandled, details with message, stackTrace, innerException.
threadsengineThe OS thread id is the DAP thread id. Names are Thread.Name; else the process's first thread is Main Thread (listed first) and the others <No name>.
stackTraceengineEvery managed frame, named Namespace.Type.Method() with the real type arguments; startFrame / levels page them. A .NET 11 runtime-async method (no state machine) is the logical stack and can be stepped across await. A frame in an assembly without symbols points at its decompiled file (see netdbg.decompile).
scopesengineOne scope, Locals. A step over a call puts <Type.Method> returned first.
variablesengineSee the value conventions. Children carry evaluateName. Static members and Raw View are nodes of their own.
evaluateengine extension relayC# expressions with the compiler's values and types (lambdas, LINQ, await waited synchronously, pointers). The relay rewrites $N object ids.
setVariableengineThe value is a C# expression.
setExpressionengineAssigns to any assignable expression.
continueengineFrozen threads stay suspended.
nextengineSteps over await to the same method's continuation.
stepInengineWith targetId, steps into the chosen call (Step Into Specific): the engine steps over the line with a breakpoint on the target.
stepOutengineFrom an async method, returns to the awaiting caller.
stepInTargetsengineThe calls of the current statement, read from the IL, in the order they run (Type.Method, properties Type.Name.get).
pauseengineStops every thread (reason pause).
gotoTargetsengineThe lines of the same method that can be the next statement.
gotoengine extension relayThe engine moves the instruction pointer; the relay sends the stopped (reason goto).
dataBreakpointInfoextension relayBreak on Value Change for a plain name. setDataBreakpoints finds the lines that write it in the workspace and sends them as netdbg.setValueWatches.
cancelengineCancels a running evaluation.
terminateengineEnds the program; exited and terminated follow.
disconnectengineEnds a launched program, detaches from an attached one (terminateDebuggee overrides).

  "netdbgSupportsApplyChanges": true,

  "supportsHitConditionalBreakpoints": true,

Custom requests and events

request netdbg.applyChanges engine

Edit and Continue: applies the saved edits of the program's C# sources to the program, without restarting (launched, not attached; a Debug build). The engine has its helper (encdelta, run with the Roslyn of the installed .NET SDK 9+) build the change against the sources as they were when debugging started, applies it with ApplyChanges, and moves breakpoints to the new code. Changed methods run the new code from their next call; a method that is running moves to the new code at its next statement unless that statement's line was changed. A running program is paused for the moment it takes. Also sends netdbg.changesApplied, output and, when applied, invalidated.

arguments

FieldTypeDescription
filesoptionalstring[]The saved files (paths as the PDB has them; the relay maps them through sourceFileMap). Omitted: every source of the program.
Example request
{
  "type": "request",
  "seq": 1,
  "command": "netdbg.applyChanges",
  "arguments": {
    "files": [
      ""
    ]
  }
}

response body

FieldTypeDescription
status"applied" | "noChanges" | "rude" | "errors" | "failed"applied, noChanges, rude (an edit that needs a restart), errors (compile errors) or failed.
messagestringOne-line summary for the user.
appliedobject[]The modules changed and how many methods each.
applied[].modulestring
applied[].methodsnumber
problemsobject[]Where an edit cannot be applied, or a compile error (line and column from 1).
problems[].filestring
problems[].linenumber
problems[].columnnumber
problems[].messagestring
detailsstring[]Further reasons, one per line (the helper could not start, the source changed before debugging, ...).
Example response
{
  "type": "response",
  "request_seq": 1,
  "success": true,
  "command": "netdbg.applyChanges",
  "body": {
    "status": "applied",
    "message": "",
    "applied": [
      {
        "module": "",
        "methods": 0
      }
    ],
    "problems": [
      {
        "file": "",
        "line": 0,
        "column": 0,
        "message": ""
      }
    ],
    "details": [
      ""
    ]
  }
}

request netdbg.coverage engine

Code coverage of the session (launch argument coverage): the rates, and with file the state of each line of that file (the editor colors them). With write, writes the Cobertura XML and the HTML report beside it now (into folder, absolute, when given).

arguments

FieldTypeDescription
fileoptionalstring
writeoptionalboolean
folderoptionalstring
Example request
{
  "type": "request",
  "seq": 1,
  "command": "netdbg.coverage",
  "arguments": {
    "file": "",
    "write": false,
    "folder": ""
  }
}

response body

FieldTypeDescription
enabledboolean
linesCoverednumber
linesValidnumber
lineRatenumber
branchesCoverednumber
branchesValidnumber
branchRatenumber
uncountableBranchesnumberBranches whose outcome cannot be counted (e.g. a switch on a computed value).
pathoptionalstringThe Cobertura XML written last.
htmloptionalstringThe HTML report of every source, written beside the Cobertura XML (<name>.coverage.html).
linesoptionalobject[]With file: each line that has code. A line that ran but did not take every branch outcome has branchesCovered < branchesValid.
lines[].linenumber
lines[].hitboolean
lines[].branchesCoveredoptionalnumber
lines[].branchesValidoptionalnumber
lines[].uncountableBranchesoptionalnumber
Example response
{
  "type": "response",
  "request_seq": 1,
  "success": true,
  "command": "netdbg.coverage",
  "body": {
    "enabled": false,
    "linesCovered": 0,
    "linesValid": 0,
    "lineRate": 0,
    "branchesCovered": 0,
    "branchesValid": 0,
    "branchRate": 0,
    "uncountableBranches": 0,
    "path": "",
    "html": "",
    "lines": [
      {
        "line": 0,
        "hit": false,
        "branchesCovered": 0,
        "branchesValid": 0,
        "uncountableBranches": 0
      }
    ]
  }
}

request netdbg.decompile engine

Decompiled sources of assemblies without symbols. The engine decompiles the application's assemblies that have no PDB (not .NET's own) itself, when they are first needed: a frame in them, a step into them, a breakpoint in a decompiled file, or this request. The C# files are written to %LOCALAPPDATA%\netdbg\decompiled\<MVID>-v<version> and the symbols are made in memory, so in the same session frames point at the files, breakpoints bind in them and locals have names. The engine then sends module (changed, symbolStatus Symbols decompiled.). Symbols found on disk or in NETDBG_SYMBOL_DIRS (downloaded ones) take precedence. Methods it cannot turn into C# are shown as IL. Without module, lists the assemblies decompiled on demand. The MCP tool decompile sends this request.

arguments

FieldTypeDescription
moduleoptionalstringFile name (MyApp.dll) or full path of a loaded assembly. Omitted: list the assemblies decompiled on demand.
typeoptionalstringWith module: a type (Namespace.Type, Type, Outer.Inner or Outer+Inner); returns the numbered lines of its file.
methodoptionalstringWith type: a member name (method, constructor = the type's name, property, event); only its lines (all overloads).
maxLinesoptionalnumberMost lines to return (default 400).
Example request
{
  "type": "request",
  "seq": 1,
  "command": "netdbg.decompile",
  "arguments": {
    "module": "",
    "type": "",
    "method": "",
    "maxLines": 0
  }
}

response body

FieldTypeDescription
modulesoptionalobject[]Without module: the assemblies decompiled on demand.
modules[].pathstring
modules[].state"notYet" | "decompiled" | "failed"
moduleoptionalstringThe assembly.
filesoptionalstring[]With module only: the decompiled files.
fileoptionalstringWith type: the file of the type, the line ranges returned (from 1, inclusive), the lines, and whether maxLines cut them.
rangesoptionalobject[]
ranges[].startLinenumber
ranges[].endLinenumber
linesoptionalobject[]
lines[].linenumber
lines[].textstring
truncatedoptionalboolean
Example response
{
  "type": "response",
  "request_seq": 1,
  "success": true,
  "command": "netdbg.decompile",
  "body": {
    "modules": [
      {
        "path": "",
        "state": "notYet"
      }
    ],
    "module": "",
    "files": [
      ""
    ],
    "file": "",
    "ranges": [
      {
        "startLine": 0,
        "endLine": 0
      }
    ],
    "lines": [
      {
        "line": 0,
        "text": ""
      }
    ],
    "truncated": false
  }
}

request netdbg.freezeThread engine

Freezes or thaws a thread: a frozen thread stays suspended across continue, steps and evaluations until thawed.

arguments

FieldTypeDescription
threadIdnumberThe thread (threads' id, the OS thread id).
frozenoptionalbooleantrue freezes (default), false thaws.
Example request
{
  "type": "request",
  "seq": 1,
  "command": "netdbg.freezeThread",
  "arguments": {
    "threadId": 0,
    "frozen": false
  }
}

response body

None (an empty body; success tells the result).

request netdbg.handleStats engine

For the types that hold a native handle in a field, counts the objects and those whose handle is not 0 (not disposed). The field may be declared by a base type (Bitmap holds Image._nativeImage).

arguments

FieldTypeDescription
fieldsobject[]The fields to look at, by declaring type (Namespace.Name) and field name.
fields[].typestring
fields[].fieldstring
Example request
{
  "type": "request",
  "seq": 1,
  "command": "netdbg.handleStats",
  "arguments": {
    "fields": [
      {
        "type": "",
        "field": ""
      }
    ]
  }
}

response body

FieldTypeDescription
typesobject[]By type name; types without one of the fields are left out.
types[].namestring
types[].countnumber
types[].livenumber
types[].fieldstring
Example response
{
  "type": "response",
  "request_seq": 1,
  "success": true,
  "command": "netdbg.handleStats",
  "body": {
    "types": [
      {
        "name": "",
        "count": 0,
        "live": 0,
        "field": ""
      }
    ]
  }
}

response body

FieldTypeDescription
typesHeapTypeStatistics[]Largest total size first. Free space between objects is counted under the name ?.
Example response

request netdbg.journal engine

The engine's journal of records made without stopping (SQL, exceptions, events, dialogs, bindings, transactions, child processes, environment). Read after a previous last with after; filter with kinds.

arguments

FieldTypeDescription
afteroptionalnumberOnly records with a higher seq (default 0: from the start of what is still kept).
kindsoptionalstring[]Record kinds (sql, exception, event, dialog, binding, transaction, process, environment). Empty: all.
limitoptionalnumberMost records to return, oldest first (default 1000).
Example request
{
  "type": "request",
  "seq": 1,
  "command": "netdbg.journal",
  "arguments": {
    "after": 0,
    "kinds": [
      ""
    ],
    "limit": 0
  }
}

response body

FieldTypeDescription
records{ [name]: any }[]Oldest first; each has seq, time, kind and the fields of that kind (a body's kind may overwrite the journal kind in the JSON).
lastnumberHighest seq written so far (also after a clear: numbers keep going).
droppednumberHow many records were discarded past the capacity (10,000).
Example response
{
  "type": "response",
  "request_seq": 1,
  "success": true,
  "command": "netdbg.journal",
  "body": {
    "records": [
      {}
    ],
    "last": 0,
    "dropped": 0
  }
}

request netdbg.makeObjectId engine

Gives the object a value refers to an id ($1) that stays valid while the program runs (a weak GC handle: it does not keep the object alive, and reads null once the object is collected). In expressions the extension writes $1 as __NETDBG_OBJID_1; values of objects with an id end with {$1}.

arguments

FieldTypeDescription
variablesReferencenumberA variable's variablesReference (from variables, evaluate or scopes).
Example request
{
  "type": "request",
  "seq": 1,
  "command": "netdbg.makeObjectId",
  "arguments": {
    "variablesReference": 0
  }
}

response body

FieldTypeDescription
idnumberThe new id (1, 2, ...); the same object asked twice keeps its first id.
Example response
{
  "type": "response",
  "request_seq": 1,
  "success": true,
  "command": "netdbg.makeObjectId",
  "body": {
    "id": 0
  }
}

request netdbg.processUsage engine

The program's process usage now, read by the engine from the process it debugs (running or stopped). The memory graph asks for it once a second.

arguments

No fields.

Example request
{
  "type": "request",
  "seq": 1,
  "command": "netdbg.processUsage",
  "arguments": {}
}

response body

FieldTypeDescription
privateBytesnumberBytes.
workingSetnumberBytes.
cpuMsnumberCPU time (kernel + user) since the process started; the usage comes from the change between two readings.
gdiObjectsnumber
userObjectsnumber
gdiQuotanumberThe per-process limits of GDI / USER objects (10,000 unless changed in the registry).
userQuotanumber
handlesnumberKernel handles.
wow64booleanA 32-bit process on 64-bit Windows: its address space is measured.
addressLimitoptionalnumberWith wow64: 2 GB, or 4 GB for a large-address-aware exe; reserved + committed bytes; the largest free block.
addressUsedoptionalnumber
largestFreeoptionalnumber
Example response
{
  "type": "response",
  "request_seq": 1,
  "success": true,
  "command": "netdbg.processUsage",
  "body": {
    "privateBytes": 0,
    "workingSet": 0,
    "cpuMs": 0,
    "gdiObjects": 0,
    "userObjects": 0,
    "gdiQuota": 0,
    "userQuota": 0,
    "handles": 0,
    "wow64": false,
    "addressLimit": 0,
    "addressUsed": 0,
    "largestFree": 0
  }
}

handlers[].breakpointNamestring

Example request
{
  "type": "request",
  "seq": 1,
  "command": "netdbg.setEventTrace",
  "arguments": {
    "handlers": [
      {
        "breakpointName": "",
        "label": "",
        "event": "",
        "control": ""
      }

  }
}

response body

request netdbg.setValueWatches engine

Break on Value Change: the names to watch and the lines that write them (the relay finds those in the workspace's C#, which the engine does not have). Replaces the earlier watches. At a write the engine reads the value, steps over the line and reads it again: when it changed it stops with reason data breakpoint (text: name: old → new), otherwise it goes on as if nothing happened. The write-site breakpoints are not reported to the client.

arguments

FieldTypeDescription
watchesobject[]Each name with its write sites (paths as the PDB has them; the relay maps them through sourceFileMap).
watches[].namestring
watches[].sitesobject[]
watches[].sites[].pathstring
watches[].sites[].linenumber
Example request
{
  "type": "request",
  "seq": 1,
  "command": "netdbg.setValueWatches",
  "arguments": {
    "watches": [
      {
        "name": "",
        "sites": [
          {
            "path": "",
            "line": 0
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}

response body

FieldTypeDescription
watchesobject[]Per name: whether a site could be bound now (sites in modules not loaded yet bind when they load), and how many sites.
watches[].namestring
watches[].verifiedboolean
watches[].sitesnumber
Example response
{
  "type": "response",
  "request_seq": 1,
  "success": true,
  "command": "netdbg.setValueWatches",
  "body": {
    "watches": [
      {
        "name": "",
        "verified": false,
        "sites": 0
      }
    ]
  }
}

event netdbg.mcpEndpoint engine

Sent once after initialize when the engine was started with --mcp-listen (setting netdbg.mcp.enabled): where AI clients can control this session through MCP (Streamable HTTP, JSON answers only). The extension offers it to VS Code's AI as an HTTP MCP server. The engine also writes it to %LOCALAPPDATA%\netdbg\mcp\<enginePid>.json (removed on exit), where netdbg --mcp-connect finds it for AI clients outside VS Code.

body

FieldTypeDescription
urlstringhttp://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp. Requests from a web page (an Origin other than localhost or VS Code) are refused.
tokenstringRequired as Authorization: Bearer <token>; made anew for every engine.
enginePidnumberProcess id of the engine.
Example event
{
  "type": "event",
  "seq": 1,
  "event": "netdbg.mcpEndpoint",
  "body": {
    "url": "",
    "token": "",
    "enginePid": 0
  }
}

event stopped engine

Standard DAP stopped. The engine sends breakpoint (also function breakpoints), step (also arriving in a Step Into Target), exception, pause (also Debugger.Break() and a UI freeze, with description), entry and data breakpoint (Break on Value Change, with description / text); the relay sends goto.

body

FieldTypeDescription
reason"breakpoint" | "step" | "exception" | "pause" | "entry" | "goto" | "data breakpoint"
threadIdnumber
allThreadsStoppedoptionalboolean
descriptionoptionalstring
textoptionalstring
hitBreakpointIdsoptionalnumber[]
Example event
{
  "type": "event",
  "seq": 1,
  "event": "stopped",
  "body": {
    "reason": "breakpoint",
    "threadId": 0,
    "allThreadsStopped": false,
    "description": "",
    "text": "",
    "hitBreakpointIds": [
      0
    ]
  }
}

Value conventions

The value / result strings of variables and evaluate. The extension parses them, so they are part of the contract.

ValuesWritten as
Objects{Namespace.Type}, or the DebuggerDisplay text; DateTime, TimeSpan, Guid and the like as {ToString()}.
Strings and charsStrings as C# literals ("a\"b"); chars as the code and the literal (120 'x').
nullnull.
Arrays and collections{int[3]}; collections with a DebuggerDisplay show it (Count = 3).
Object idsA value with an id ends with {$N}; in expressions $N is sent as __NETDBG_OBJID_N.
EnumsMember names (Read, Write for flags); unnamed values as the number in the underlying type (-6).
PointersThe pointed value, with the pointer type in type (int*); null for 0.
Exceptions from evaluationsThe result is the exception object ({System.InvalidOperationException}); errors fail the request with a message saying what to do.
Void callsExpression has been evaluated and has no value with type void.

Shared types

ExpressionEvaluationOptions

The same option as the C# extension's debugger (vsdbg).

FieldTypeDescription
allowImplicitFuncEvaloptionalbooleanRun property getters and ToString() / DebuggerDisplay to show values (default true). When false, properties come with presentationHint.lazy and run only when expanded; explicit evaluations (watch, hover, console) still run code.

HeapTypeStatistics

FieldTypeDescription
namestringType name as the Variables view shows it (System.Collections.Generic.List<int>).
countnumberNumber of objects.
sizenumberTotal size in bytes.
